headline: House holds Leon Black in contempt of Congress
summary: The House on Wednesday held billionaire Leon Black in contempt of Congress and referred him to the Justice Department. Black defied Oversight Committee subpoenas to appear and turn over documents in its investigation into Jeffrey Epstein. He is challenging the subpoenas in court. His lawyers say he had no knowledge of Epstein's conduct.

cover_question.q: What if you say no to Congress?

cover_answer: It can become a crime. The Justice Department decides.
table_question: Can you refuse to answer questions if you think they're unfair?

5-7.script: Congress is a big group of grown-ups who make the country's rules. They told a very rich man to come and answer questions. He didn't come. So they said he broke the rule, like a kid being sent to the office for skipping class. The grown-ups have it.
5-7.why: Skipping when you're called is something they understand. What the questions were about can wait.

8-12.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
8-12.script: A House committee is investigating Jeffrey Epstein, a financier convicted of sex crimes, now dead. It ordered Leon Black, who did business with him, to answer questions. He refused. So the House held him in contempt, like a referee sending a call up to the league.
8-12.why: Order, refusal, referral. A chain they can follow.

13-17.script: Is "I had no knowledge" a reason to skip a subpoena? Leon Black's lawyers say he knew nothing of Epstein's conduct and Congress is abusing its power. Both parties on the committee said show up anyway. Who should settle that, Congress or a judge?
13-17.why: The fairness of the process is what they will argue about. Let them.

5-7.a: No. Congress said he broke a rule by not showing up. Other grown-ups will decide what happens next.

8-12.q: What if you say no to Congress?
8-12.a: Contempt of Congress. The Justice Department decides whether to charge you.
A financier convicted of sex crimes, now dead. Black did business with him.

13-17.q: Is "I had no knowledge" a reason to skip a subpoena?
13-17.a: His lawyers say yes and call it an abuse of power. The committee said no.
Unknown. The Justice Department decides. Comer says no one is above the law.
